A1.justification: Both complete 16-page PDFs describe SegQuant. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison. Appendix pages 10–16 are identical in extracted text and rendered appearance.

before.justification: v1 reports original quantization experiments, including benchmark comparisons in Tables 2 and 5–7, component ablations in Tables 3–4, and efficiency measurements in Figure 10.

after.justification: v4 retains these original benchmark results, ablations, efficiency measurements, and qualitative comparisons in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: SegQuant retains the same SegLinear input/output segmentation, DualScale activation quantization, and optimizer/calibrator framework. No algorithm, component, or inference procedure changes.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same image-generation coverage using COCO, MJHQ-30K, and DCI, with SD3.5, SDXL, FLUX, and the same ControlNet analyses. No dataset, task, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in corresponding quantitative and qualitative comparisons, including Q-Diffusion, PTQD, PTQ4DiT, TAC-Diffusion, and SVDQuant. Updating the GPTQ reference to its OPTQ publication title does not change the evaluated method.

E3.justification: Evaluation metrics, model configurations, precision settings, calibration sample counts, and sampling procedures remain unchanged. Both versions specify 50 sampling steps and retain the same appendix guidance scale, quantization granularity, and baseline settings.

E4.justification: The time-versus-latent sensitivity analysis, polarity analysis, SegLinear/DualScale ablations, efficiency comparison, and qualitative examples are retained with the same evidence. Tables 3–4 and the supplementary visual analyses contain no additions or revisions.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed lists, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Point-estimate reporting and the 30-timestep averaging used for activation statistics are unchanged.

E6.justification: Numerical entries in Tables 1–7, Figure 10 efficiency measurements, and qualitative outputs match. For example, Table 2 retains SegQuant-G FID values of 12.37 for SD3.5 W8A8 and 7.78 for FLUX W4A8.

T1.justification: The SegLinear decompositions, DualScale definitions, and appendix Quantization Recovery Comparison derivations are unchanged. No mathematical assumptions, propositions, proofs, or substantive derivations are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about semantic segmentation, polarity preservation, generation quality, architectural generalization, and deployment compatibility. Minor wording edits do not change their scope.

C2.justification: Interpretations of time-related sensitivity, semantic partitioning, negative activations, and quality-versus-runtime tradeoffs remain unchanged. No substantive limitation, failure condition, or applicability qualification is added or removed.

D1.justification: Hardware information and implementation disclosures are retained, including RTX 4090/L20 GPUs, the SmoothQuant alpha sweep, SVDQuant rank 64, and baseline calibration details. The CUTLASS reference and released-codebase statement are unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning remain the same. References such as GPTQ/OPTQ, ViDiT-Q, COCO, and SDXL receive publication-title, venue, year, or author-metadata updates; these do not introduce different works or revise novelty claims.

P1.justification: The author list changes and corresponding-author markers are added. The introduction changes 'spatial semantic variations' to 'spatial and semantic variations,' and bibliography metadata is updated. Nearly all prose and the section sequence remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 2 moves from the lower-left to the upper-right of page 3. Spacing and text flow shift other placements, including Table 3 and the conclusion. Figure/table content and captions are retained, and appendix layouts are identical.

improvement.justification: v4 provides limited editorial and bibliographic updates with modest layout adjustments. The methods, empirical evidence, interpretations, and reproducibility information remain unchanged, and the appendices are identical. These edits do not materially improve or diminish the paper's clarity or scientific support.
